display.purpose: Hero line only. The page's largest voice.

body.purpose: Reading copy, ~70ch measure, line-height 1.75 for dark reading.

label.purpose: Section label, hero eyebrow, dates, tags, fact labels. Geist Mono, uppercase, tracked.

motion.name: ease-out-quint
motion.purpose: Confident ease-out for the hero reveal (eyebrow, glow, disclosure). No bounce.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Alternate ease-out curve for sharper entrances.

components.name: Link
components.description: The primary interactive element. The site is link-led, not button-led; links are cobalt and brighten to ink on hover.
components.html: Why I build with Astro islands
components.css: .ds-link { color: oklch(0.66 0.15 252); text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 0.2em; transition: color 0.16s ease; } .ds-link:hover { color: oklch(0.95 0.006 252); } .ds-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(0.66 0.15 252); outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 2px; }

components.name: Brand Wordmark
components.description: The site wordmark: ink text with a single cobalt period.
components.css: .ds-brand { font-family: 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 900; font-size: 1.25rem; letter-spacing: -0.03em; color: oklch(0.95 0.006 252); text-decoration: none; } .ds-brand-dot { color: oklch(0.66 0.15 252); }

components.name: Nav Link
components.description: Header navigation: muted at rest, cobalt on hover.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { font-family: 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.95rem; color: oklch(0.72 0.012 252); text-decoration: none; transition: color 0.16s ease; } .ds-nav-link:hover { color: oklch(0.66 0.15 252); }

components.name: Post Card
components.description: A tappable row on the room background. No card at rest; lifts to the panel tint on hover and the title shifts to cobalt.
components.html: Why I Build Content Sites With Astro IslandsMay 30, 2026
components.css: .ds-post-card { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr auto; align-items: baseline; gap: 0.5rem 1rem; text-decoration: none; padding: 1rem 0.75rem; border-radius: 10px; transition: background 0.18s ease; } .ds-post-card:hover { background: oklch(0.205 0.022 252); } .ds-post-title { font-family: 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 1.25rem; letter-spacing: -0.02em; color: oklch(0.95 0.006 252); transition: color 0.18s ease; } .ds-post-card:hover .ds-post-title { color: oklch(0.66 0.15 252); } .ds-post-date { font-family: 'Geist Mono Variable', ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 0.8rem; color: oklch(0.58 0.014 252); white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Tag
components.description: Outlined mono readout, not a filled badge. Muted text inside a 1px line border, fully pill-rounded. The old yellow tag is retired.
components.css: .ds-tag { font-family: 'Geist Mono Variable', ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 0.72rem; color: oklch(0.72 0.012 252); border: 1px solid oklch(0.32 0.022 252); border-radius: 999px; padding: 0.1rem 0.55rem; }

components.name: Blockquote
components.description: No side stripe. A quiet full-border panel on the surface tint with muted italic text. Replaces the banned border-left:3px stripe.
components.html: The trick isn't doing more on the client. It's hydrating only what moves.
components.css: .ds-quote { margin: 1.75rem 0; padding: 1rem 1.25rem; background: oklch(0.205 0.022 252); border: 1px solid oklch(0.32 0.022 252); border-radius: 10px; color: oklch(0.72 0.012 252); font-style: italic; font-size: 1.12rem; }

components.name: Inline Code
components.description: Geist Mono on the panel tint with a 1px line border.
components.css: .ds-code { font-family: 'Geist Mono Variable', ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 0.88em; background: oklch(0.205 0.022 252); padding: 0.15em 0.4em; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid oklch(0.32 0.022 252); color: oklch(0.95 0.006 252); }

components.name: Section Label
components.description: The single tracked-uppercase mono label allowed on a reading page (e.g. 'Writing', 'About'). Used sparingly, never as per-section grammar.
components.css: .ds-section-label { font-family: 'Geist Mono Variable', ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 0.78rem; letter-spacing: 0.18em; text-transform: uppercase; color: oklch(0.58 0.014 252); margin: 0 0 1.25rem; }

narrative.overview: A personal blog and portfolio where the design IS the product. The whole site lives in one room: a dark, cobalt-tinted space lit by the glow of a display at blue hour, with one warm amber light playing against the cool dark. The hero reads the visitor's browser and reports it back like a navigational instrument; the reading pages are the calm after, lit by the same cobalt, in the same Geist. Built from one committed move done impeccably: a single cobalt seed generates every surface and link, a single amber accent plays the warm light, and one typeface (Geist sans + mono) carries the whole site through weight and scale contrast. Depth is tonal layering, not shadow. It rejects the generic-blog template, the dark-purple-gradient SaaS clone, trying-too-hard maximalism, and the AI-default warm-cream-plus-muted-slate-plus-tracked-eyebrow editorial scaffolding.
keyCharacteristics: One dark cobalt room, sitewide — the hero is continuous with the page, not a separate panel.
One typeface, Geist (sans + mono), carrying hierarchy through weight and scale.
Cobalt does the structural work (links, brand, the payoff); amber is the rare warm highlight.
Depth by tonal layering, not shadow. Surfaces are flat at rest.
Body text at 7-16:1 contrast — generously lit, never muted-gray-on-tint.
Calm by default. The hero is the showpiece; reading pages get out of the way.

rules.name: The One Room Rule
rules.body: The whole site shares one background (oklch(0.17 0.018 252)). The hero is the same room, lit, not a panel pasted onto a different page. A second base background reintroduces the two-sites seam.

rules.name: The Beam Rule
rules.body: Amber appears on ≤5% of any screen. It is the one warm light in a cool room; its rarity is the point. The moment amber does structural work it has stopped being the lighthouse beam.

rules.name: The No-Vermilion Rule
rules.body: No hot vermilion (#ff5c39), no warm yellow (#ffd23f), no warm-cream (#fbf7f2), no Inter. Those were the old starter layer; one stray reference reads as AI slop.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Geist carries the entire site. Hierarchy comes from weight (400/600/700/800) and scale (≥1.25 steps), never a second display face.

rules.name: The Dark-Reading Rule
rules.body: Light text on the dark room reads lighter; prose line-height is set at 1.75 so the measure stays calm and legible.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. State responds with a tonal shift (bg to surface) or a color shift, never a shadow appearing.

dos: Do build every surface from the cobalt seed and keep the whole site on one background (oklch(0.17 0.018 252)).
Do use cobalt for links, brand, and interactive emphasis; reserve amber for the rare warm highlight (≤5%).
Do keep body text at ≥4.5:1 (it runs 7-16:1 here); push close colors toward ink.
Do carry the whole site in Geist; build hierarchy from weight and scale.
Do convey depth with tonal layering, never a drop shadow.
Do keep the reading experience calm: ~70ch measure, prose line-height 1.75, zero gimmicks.
Do give the hero its one bloom and one motion sequence, and nothing else competes with it.
donts: Don't reintroduce the retired starter layer: no vermilion #ff5c39, no yellow #ffd23f, no warm-cream #fbf7f2, no Inter.
Don't use the AI-default warm-cream + muted-slate + tracked-eyebrow-over-every-section editorial scaffolding.
Don't use border-left/border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe (the banned side-stripe).
Don't ship generic-blog-template chrome (Medium / Substack / dev.to default themes).
Don't build dark-purple-gradient SaaS clones, hero-metric stat blocks, or build-faster-ship-faster cadence.
Don't pile on maximalism: animation on every scroll, glassmorphism everywhere, effects with no purpose.
Don't let muted gray sit on the tinted dark as body copy; faint is for labels and dates only.
Don't add drop shadows. If a surface needs to lift, tint it up.
